explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem says that the parabolic cocycles of Γ₀(N) with values in integral binary forms of degree n form a finitely generated ℤ-module. Its content depends on the library's own definitions: `coeffParabolicCocycles`, `binaryFormRepSL`, `BinaryForm`, `coeffCocycles_eq_of_eqOn` and the instance `instGroupFG_Gamma0`. Mathlib has no theory of parabolic cocycles or of this binary-form representation that would contain the statement. The proof combines several steps: it takes a finite generating set of Γ₀(N), maps each cocycle to its values on those generators (an injective map), and uses Noetherianity of the target together with `Module.Finite.of_injective`. Those general Mathlib lemmas are only ingredients, not a single declaration that carries the result. I identified this from the library-specific definitions without running a separate search of Mathlib.
